_comment: Tier-1 static regression checks. Pure substring grep over repo files — zero model tokens, deterministic, run on every change. 'forbidden' patterns must not appear (optionally limited by 'in' path-substring); 'required' patterns must appear in the file(s) whose path contains 'in'. These encode PROJECT CONVENTIONS, some of which are stricter than raw SAP rules (noted per rule).

rules.note: Project convention: RAP audit 'created at' is a timestamp -> @Semantics.systemDateTime.createdAt. @Semantics.systemDate.* is valid in SAP only for genuine date-only fields; do not use it for audit semantics here. (grounding-protocol.md is excluded: it discusses this very anti-pattern as a worked example.)
Same convention as createdAt: audit 'last changed at' is a timestamp -> @Semantics.systemDateTime.lastChangedAt.
The annotations reference must teach the correct timestamp audit annotation.
RAP projection contract must be documented.
The unmanaged/additional save saver base class must be documented.
xsdbool vs boolc guidance must be present.
ABAP SQL test double must be documented.
The MOVE-CORRESPONDING-vs-CORRESPONDING# BASE trap must be documented.
The reference must document that @Semantics.systemDate.* is for date-only fields (not a blanket 'never systemDate'); systemDateTime is the RAP audit-timestamp standard.

The action skill must warn that COMMIT ENTITIES/COMMIT WORK inside a handler or saver dumps with this runtime error (grounded: github.com/SAP-samples/abap-cheat-sheets 17_SAP_LUW.md, 'modify transactional phase' example).

Project convention: when a RAP action needs to modify AND commit another BO independently, teach the CL_ABAP_PARALLEL isolation pattern (own aRFC session/LUW) alongside same-LUW EML (default) and bgPF (after-commit async).
The parallel-processing skill must document the RAP commit-isolation use case (committing another BO from a behavior implementation via a worker task) with its consistency caveat.
Publishing convention: skills/agents/docs must cite public GitHub URLs (github.com/SAP-samples/...), never the local example/ mirror folder — it is deleted before the repo is published.

Publishing convention: no machine-local absolute paths (a Windows user-profile directory) in published content; cite public URLs instead. Pattern is drive-and-user agnostic so it catches any contributor's path, and embeds no real username.
Root CLAUDE.md must wire the superpowers development loop (brainstorming stage marker). Covered via scanFiles since CLAUDE.md lives outside scanDirs.

rules.pattern: Your place in the development process
rules.note: The developer agent must carry the stage-note subsection tying it to the superpowers development loop.

Project policy: abap-clean-style is active before any ABAP generation, not only when the task maps to the style row. Locked after a review found the load was conditional and single-letter identifiers slipped into generated code. Now enforced structurally — abap-clean-style must sit in the developer agent's `skills:` frontmatter so its full content (incl. the naming grid) is preloaded into the subagent at startup, independent of any Skill-tool call.

Independent lock on the naming-convention instruction paragraph itself (separate from the frontmatter-membership check above) — a prior external redesign deleted this whole paragraph while leaving the frontmatter check passing under a rewritten pattern, so the two checks must not share one point of failure.

rules.pattern: Design names to the shipped naming convention
rules.note: The architect must propose names per the shipped naming convention, not Clean ABAP's prefix-free default, before development starts.
The reviewer must judge naming against the shipped Hungarian convention, not flag it as a Clean ABAP violation.

A bare COMMIT ENTITIES with no RESPONSE OF/FAILED/REPORTED discards the outcome and models committing without asserting anything. Where a test genuinely needs to cross the save sequence (e.g. testing an on-save determination), use COMMIT ENTITIES RESPONSE OF ... FAILED ... REPORTED ... and assert on the result, as in determine_sets_audit_fields_on_save.

Managed numbering keys are available in MAPPED without a commit; committing here only to read failed_commit/reported_commit models an unnecessary commit in a test. A test that genuinely needs to assert a save-sequence outcome should use a distinctly-named FAILED/REPORTED target (e.g. failed_save) scoped to that specific test.

Hashed-table traversal order is unspecified/implementation-defined per the ABAP Keyword Documentation, not a guaranteed insertion order. Use a sorted table or an explicit secondary sorted key when order matters.
Same convention as internal-tables-no-hashed-insertion-order-claim, locking references/operations.md's differently-worded (pre-fix) phrasing of the same claim.
assert_text_matches is a real cl_abap_unit_assert method (see references/assert-cheatsheet.md); SKILL.md previously denied its existence, contradicting the cheatsheet in the same skill.
MAX(key)+index numbering is racy under concurrent saves. Use cl_numberrange_runtime=>number_get (see rap-saves-and-numbering's late-numbering-adjust-numbers.abap) instead of a demo MAX-based pattern.
Lesson 2026-09-17: navigate_to_optional returns the narrow entity01 interface; bind_action has no cast guard, so the downcast is the fix — not a raw-HTTP rewrite.
The 'Property X cannot be used for …' business-message pattern must stay documented as a payload (not transport) failure.
if_apj_rt_run (public attributes, F4 in the SAJC entry) must be documented as the F4-capable job contract.
Job date/time parameters are compared against UTC persistence; converting with the user zone shifts the window.
get_user_time_zone( ) is the executing user's zone (the technical job user in a job) — must stay stated.
T100 placeholders are 50 chars; exceptions carrying diagnostics need the mv_long_text / get_long_text channel.
Interface doubles prove our logic only; the serialization test + live smoke obligation must stay.
/ui2/cl_json compress semantics: only empty strings are omitted; '0' and initial dates survive.

rules.pattern: Ask once per task whether you may activate
rules.note: The ADT edit tool does not activate and says not to unless asked; activation stays a confirmed step, never a side effect of editing.
A runtime-error entry can carry business data; only the error class, statement and call stack may leave the session.
The developer must know the live ADT rules (destination first, real test output, activation and transport confirmation).
The architect grounds designs in the real system through the read-only ADT tools.
The reviewer uses ATC and unit-test output from the system as evidence.

rules.pattern: You review; you do not change the system.
rules.note: An independent gate must not edit, activate or file ATC exemptions through the ADT tools it was given for evidence.
New objects need a package, a transport and confirmed names before the first line is written; without a named gate the developer starts building and asks later.
The package is part of the intake: never invented or defaulted, because it decides ownership and which transport applies.
A new object in a transportable package must be recorded on a request the user named; the number is asked for up front, not discovered at activation.
Local packages ($TMP) carry no transport request; the gate must say so, or the developer blocks on a number that cannot exist.

rules.pattern: a table of every object you are about to create
rules.note: Concrete object names, not only the convention, are proposed for confirmation before development starts.
The ADT create and generator tools take a transport number and write to a package; the guide must hold the same package, transport and names gate as the developer agent.
The generator misfire lesson must point at the tool the ADT MCP server really exposes (3.62.0), or the agent looks for a tool that is not there.

Not a tool of the ADT MCP server any more; the generator tools are abap_objects_generator_list, _get_schema and _run. (The ABAP method of that name in the XCO example is unrelated and outside this path.)

rules.pattern: The commit boundary follows the call stack
rules.note: Real incident: an agent put COMMIT ENTITIES in a helper class that an action calls. It compiled, passed activation and tests, and is only wrong at runtime. The rule is about what runs while a handler or saver is on the stack, not about which class holds the statement, and it must sit in the first screen of the skill, where agents stop reading.

rules.pattern: only if your code is the top of the call stack
rules.note: The consumer workflow's commit step was unconditional (step 5); it must be conditional on the caller context.

rules.pattern: inside handler/saver methods or any code they call
rules.note: 'Inside handler/saver methods' read as lexical; a helper class called from a handler is the same violation. The pattern is unique to the Not-allowed bullet, so removing that bullet's wording fails the rule.
Agents read the first ~100 lines of a skill; the no-commit-in-handlers rule cannot live only in the EML section at line ~280.

rules.pattern: inside another BO's handler or saver
rules.note: MODIFY ENTITIES ... COMMIT ENTITIES is the unit of work for top-level consumers only.

rules.pattern: Pattern: `MODIFY ENTITIES … COMMIT ENTITIES` is the unit of work.
rules.note: The unqualified sentence taught the commit pattern without saying it is wrong inside handlers, savers and anything they call.

rules.pattern: non-framework code (tests, batch jobs, other BOs)
rules.note: 'Other BOs' means other BOs' handlers, which must not commit; the sentence invited exactly that.

The commit-under-a-handler guard only exists if the plugin registers it; both Claude Code and VS Code read hooks/hooks.json.

Reading the cluster file at run time cost a 12k-character read and was skipped in practice; its cues are rendered into the agent by scripts/build_agent_routing.py.
A controlled bgPF operation (if_bgmc_op_single) must not commit; abap-background-processing says so. Only an uncontrolled one may.
The top-of-call-stack list must name the one kind of bgPF operation that may commit.
The confirmation text must not tell the user that any bgPF worker may commit.
SAP's cheat sheet says contract violations 'result in a runtime error (or are logged)'; the skill must not claim a dump on every release.
Free-to-do must state the real boundary now that the agent edits objects through the ADT tools: development destination after the intake, never production.

A version in plugin.json pins Claude Code users to that string until someone changes it: tested end to end, `claude plugin update` answers 'already at the latest version' however many commits are pushed. Without it Claude Code uses the commit SHA, so every merge to main is an update. (VS Code updates by pulling the repository and does not need it.)
GitHub shows ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} links as dead 'undefined' URLs and VS Code does not substitute the placeholder in agent text. Write the path as inline code instead; Claude Code still fills it in.
Copilot does not fill in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; the agent must be told how to find the plugin root (the folder that holds .claude/skills/), or every doc path in the agent is unusable there.
